story_type: hurricane seen from the space station before landfall
hook: Space station cameras watched this hurricane spin up.
narration: Space station cameras watched this hurricane spin up over the Gulf of Mexico.
August twenty ninth, twenty twenty three. Hurricane Idalia, two hundred sixty miles below.
It was a Category 1 with eighty five mile an hour winds, expected to hit Florida as a Category 3 or stronger.
Warm Gulf water is the fuel. The storm draws up heat and moisture, and the winds tighten around the eye.
[short pause] Forecasters warned of a life-threatening storm surge along Florida's Big Bend.
outcome: The next morning, Idalia made landfall in the Florida Big Bend as an extremely dangerous Category 3 hurricane.

location_card.place: Gulf of Mexico, from the ISS

title: Hurricane Idalia seen from space
description:
International Space Station cameras captured Hurricane Idalia over the eastern Gulf of Mexico on Aug. 29, 2023, as it strengthened toward Florida. The next morning the National Hurricane Center reported Idalia made landfall in the Florida Big Bend as a Category 3 hurricane.

Footage: NASA JSC video, via the NASA Image and Video Library: https://images.nasa.gov/details/Expedition_69_Space_Station_Flies_Over_Hurricane_Idalia_Live

facts.claim: Station cameras captured strengthening Idalia on Aug. 29, 2023, from 260 miles up
facts.source_quote: External cameras on the International Space Station captured views of a strengthening Hurricane Idalia at 11:35 a.m. EDT on Tuesday, Aug. 29, 2023 as the station flew 260 miles overhead.
